To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the mutual information in a multi-unit response depends on the degree of overlap of the attribute-specific information in the constituent single-units, that the mutual information is greater than or equal to the maximum of the single-unit mutual information rates, and that the information in the multi-units is not lost completely when the units are superimposing.

the mutual information in a multi-unit signal is the maximum of the constituent single units' information rates, and that the normalized gain in multi-unit information over single units is a function of the degree of similarity of the single-unit information rates.
the information of a multi-unit signal is a function of the information in the single-unit spike train responses and the similarity in the attribute specific information of the single units.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of how the brain processes information.
the problem of information transmission by a population of neurons.
the analysis of information transmission in multi-unit neural responses.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the information content of the multi-unit response depends on the similarity of the attribute-specific information in the individual units and that the degree of similarity depends on the degree to which the units' encoding is independent.
information in single-unit spike trains is not completely lost, but can be preserved in multi-unit responses.
multi-unit information can be greater or less than the sum of the constituent single units, depending on the degree of confounding in the single units' responses.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the absence of confounding information in the single-unit spike responses, the information in multi-unit recordings is equal to the sum of the information contained in the constituent single-unit responses.

, when the information in constituent single-unit spike-train responses is similar, the union of these responses can fully recover single-unit information, and even reduce the confounding information present.
the information content of the multi-unit signal depends on the degree of overlap in the single-unit responses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
information is not lost when multiple units fire in response to a stimulus and that it may even be possible to recover the information in the single-unit spike train from a multi-unit response.
the information in multi-unit signals is not necessarily a fraction of the information in the corresponding single units.
the information in multi-unit responses is not necessarily less than that in the constituent units.
